summary: The returned tree must contain one newly constructed node for every traversal value, so linear work is unavoidable. The position-map reconstruction creates each node once with constant-time splits.

optimality.argument: The result is an n-node binary tree, and constructing its n distinct node objects requires Omega(n) time. The candidate builds the inorder position map in O(n), consumes each preorder value once, performs one constant-time position lookup per node, and creates exactly one node per value, for O(n) total time and O(n) total map, output, and recursion storage.

replacement_checks.evidence: Materializing the required n-node result requires at least one construction action for each node.
The position map is built once, and each preorder value causes one lookup, one node construction, and two disjoint recursive interval calls.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a branching tree and the one-node minimum; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
